# The Problem


The CRAN packages for Likert-type data workflow, viz, @mollazehi2025; @winzar2026 and @bryer2025, have not contemplated a situation whereby transliterated to other formats may be required for more robust interpretation. They effectively facilitate standard Likert scale workflows, but operate under the assumption that data is conventional, clean ordinal format lacking the architectural framework required to handle format transliteration.

Empirical workflow may encounter non-standard data requiring transformation for deep interpretation. For instance, researchers may need to convert Likert-type responses into ordinal scales and vice versa, or synthesize valid Likert-type scales from non-Likert data. Existing workflow cannot execute these transformations natively, therefore, work rely on disjointed, manual workarounds and ad-hoc scripting. This fragmentation disrupts workflows, introduces data entry risks and errors, resulting in man-hours loss. This project proposes an open-source R package for transliteration and dynamic format conversion to fill the gap and eliminate manual data workflows, preserve data integrity, and optimize workflow for handling non-standard Likert-type workflows.
